thread:
alex: FYI rolled out role schema migration to prod at 09:12 UTC and kicked off legacy-role backfill. quick sanity check: the backfill touched service-account mappings.

maria: getting a spike of alerts from our analytics buckets — a single service account `ml-batch` is issuing many s3:GetObject calls to analytics-prod/etl/ — not expected

alex: that sounds bad. list of changes in the migration:
```json
{"mappings": [{"old_role":"analytics_reader_v1","new_role":"analytics_viewer"}, {"old_role":"ml_worker","new_role":"ml_batch"}]}
```
I did include a one-time ACL mapping for a legacy group. Could be misapplied.

tim: can we pause the backfill job and revert the mapping that added `ml-batch` -> analytics_viewer? If backfill is incremental, we should stop before more principals are updated.

jordan: I paused the backfill at 09:16 UTC (killed the job). Deployment still active though. I can revert the mapping in IAM service config and push a patch.

elaine: running audit query to see how many objects were accessed and which principals read them.

deploy-bot: rollback request acknowledged. Starting config revert: rollback-id=rb-2026-03-20-09-17. Estimated 30s.

maria: logs show ~3,200 GETs from ml-batch to analytics-prod between 09:12–09:18. Most are small parquet files. No writes observed.

alex: good catch. no writes is reassuring. still need to treat as data exposure. timeline: 09:12 migration + backfill start, 09:16 backfill paused, 09:17 revert pushed, 09:18 revert applied.

tim: immediate mitigation checklist:
- revoke session tokens for `ml-batch` (done?)
- rotate service-account keys if long lived
- ensure KMS grants didn't change
- run scan to list objects accessed

jordan: revoked active sessions for ml-batch at 09:20 UTC. Key rotation scheduled — will coordinate with infra to rotate short-lived creds for that SA.

elaine: KMS IAM policy unaffected; the KMS key grant table shows no extra principals. access was via S3 ACLs/IAM mapping only.

maria: starting object access listing now, will produce a minimal dataset of object paths and requestor IPs. putting results in #sec-incident with restricted viewers.

alex: who else touched the migration PR? we need to audit the change to the mapping logic that caused legacy groups to map to broader role.

tim: PR was #842 by me but I missed a join condition — mapping used `OR` instead of `AND` when matching legacy tags. that would match both `ml_worker` and `analytics` groups.

alex: ok actionable: revert PR + fix join condition + add unit test and integration test that simulates backfill.

jordan: I've created a follow-up hotfix PR and will only allow it after we confirm backfill is aborted and audit data is captured. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/899

deploy-bot: revert complete. roll id rb-2026-03-20-09-17 finished. No further backfill jobs will run until manual resume.

elaine: preliminary audit: 3,214 objects read by ml-batch, requestor IPs mostly internal cluster IPs. No external egress observed. tagging incident as P2 for now. I'll prepare a short incident summary.

maria: sending customer-facing note draft to legal for review; we need to decide if disclosure is required given internal-only access. tagging @legal.

alex: timeline and mitigations look good. follow-ups:
- postmortem with root cause and test coverage changes
- add a safety check to backfill that disallows granting access to analytics-prod buckets unless approved
- rotate any long-lived SA keys and confirm no external tokens were used

tim: adding a schema migration gate to require a preview of affected principals and a dry-run report before backfill executes.

jordan: will also add alerting rule: spike in cross-role S3 reads from a single principal triggers immediate pager to sec-oncall.

elaine: uploading audit CSV to secure drive and creating a findings doc. tagging in #incidents once ready.

alex: thanks everyone. keep updates short in this thread. we'll schedule a blameless postmortem tomorrow morning.
